text:
ashley: Hey team — ACME on private VPC is seeing intermittent 502s and we're not receiving their audit logs. Customer says this started right after they applied a stricter inbound policy. Can security confirm if our control-plane callers need any specific inbound rules?

ben: Thanks. Do we have a quick repro or packet-level evidence? Which endpoint is failing (control-plane -> customer or customer -> control-plane)?

ashley: Control-plane -> customer. Their webhook endpoint is returning RSTs. I grabbed a tcpdump from our side during a failed POST to https://acme-vpc.internal.redwood/audit (we use our control-plane egress IPs). Snippet: `TCP 52.12.34.56:443 > 10.10.4.12:443 RST` and `curl -v --cert client.pem https://10.10.4.12/v1/audit` -> `* handshake: TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS alert, unknown CA` then connection reset.

carlos: Unknown CA + RST suggests the customer's firewall/proxy might be terminating TLS or requiring a specific SNI or client CA. For private deployments we do mutual TLS to their ingress. Did they rotate their client CA or enable a proxy that does TLS termination?

sam: Oncall checked the control-plane logs: `POST /v1/audit 502 connection reset by peer` at 2026-02-12T16:12Z. No retry succeeded. Also noticed their KMS calls from the host are failing later (HSM errors) — possibly separate but likely related to network policy changes.

ashley: Customer confirms they added a default-deny inbound rule and only allowed a handful of IP ranges. They allowed 10.0.0.0/8 for their internal infra but did not add our control-plane egress IPs. They asked what exact IPs and ports we need and whether we can avoid IP allowlisting by switching to an outbound mTLS tunnel.

ben: For immediate unblock, they need to allow our control-plane egress IP list (current: `52.12.34.56`, `52.12.34.57`, `52.12.34.58`) on TCP/443 and permit SNI `control-plane.redwood-inference.com`. Additionally, healthcheck probes use `/healthz` on 443 from same IPs. For audit ingestion we POST to `/v1/audit` and require client mTLS (client cert subject CN=redwood-control).

carlos: Security notes: we cannot publish IPs in public docs but will provide them in the private onboarding checklist. Recommend least-priv rules: allow only the three IPs on 443 to their audit endpoint, and drop everything else. If they insist on not allowing IPs, we can negotiate establishing an outbound TLS tunnel or customer-initiated proxy (pull model) so they don't need to open inbound at all. That requires changes in our deployment model and an onboarding run.

ashley: Also seeing KMS issues in their logs: `Error: HSM unreachable` during keywrap. They run a cloud HSM that requires outbound to `kms.cloudprovider.net:443` from the host. This is probably outbound being blocked on their side (egress default-deny), not inbound.

sam: Actionable triage checklist I propose: 1) Ask customer to add allowlist for control-plane egress IPs + SNI on 443; 2) Confirm their TLS stack accepts our client cert chain (we can repro with `openssl s_client -connect <host>:443 -servername control-plane.redwood-inference.com -cert client.pem -key client.key`); 3) Check host egress to cloud KMS endpoints for HSM errors; 4) Update onboarding runbook with explicit firewall/snippet.

ashley: I posted the exact `iptables`-style example they can paste into their FW: `allow tcp from 52.12.34.56/32 to 10.10.4.12/32 port 443 proto tcp; allow tcp from 52.12.34.57/32 to 10.10.4.12/32 port 443 proto tcp` and also remind them to allow return traffic.

carlos: Two security caveats: - Don't rely on IPs alone long-term; IPs can change — use mTLS with cert pinning or set up an enterprise VPN/peering. - Ensure audit logs are retained per contract; if audit ingestion was down, we need to confirm retention and replay capability.

ashley: Customer asked for a replay path. ben — can we replay buffered audit logs into their VPC after they open the inbound rule, or do we need to pull a webhook?

ben: We buffer locally for up to 24 hours in the control-plane. We can re-POST once connectivity restored, but if they had a strict firewall that drops retransmitted packets, better to do a scheduled replay with retries and exponential backoff. I'll prepare a small script to resend `POST /v1/audit` files from the buffer.

carlos: I'll approve a temporary exception to share the control-plane IPs with ACME support for setup. After they confirm, we should schedule a hardening call to switch them to mTLS pinning or private peering. Also add a checklist item to our Private/VPC security review doc: verify inbound allowlist + client CA fingerprints + KMS egress.

deploy-bot: [deploy] rollout/producer-audit-retry v2 triggered by @ben — retry window=24h

ashley: I'll send the allowlist + `openssl s_client` repro steps to the customer and request screenshots of firewall deny logs showing `REJECT` or `RST`. If they provide the logs, we can confirm CA mismatch vs firewall drop.

sam: TL;DR and owners: - Immediate unblock: ashley -> get logs from customer and have them add 52.12.34.56/57/58:443 allowlist (ashley owns) - Replay buffered audits: ben -> run retry job and watch for success (ben owns) - Security follow-up: carlos -> approve IP share and schedule hardening call (carlos owns)

ashley: noted. pinging @acme-eng to request the change now. :thumbsup:

carlos: Thanks everyone. I'll drop a short blurb in the Private/VPC runbook and link to the onboarding checklist.

ben: I'll also add a small FAQ entry under 'networking' that lists the minimal inbound/outbound rules for private deployments.

ashley: Closing loop once customer confirms no more 502s. :white_check_mark:
